न्यूज शो देखना पसंद है. जितनी रात होती जाती है, शो उतने ही पागलपन भरे होते जाते हैं.” उन्होंने कहा, “शाम छह बजे एक शो में आठ लोग बहस कर रहे होते हैं. रात 10 बजे 12 लोग एक साथ बोल रहे होते हैं. आप हुई मुलाकात से जुड़ा एक अहम दावा भी किया. उनके मुताबिक, भारतीय विदेश मंत्रालय ने बैठक से पहले मीडिया को केवल दोनों नेताओं की शुरुआती टिप्पणियां रिकॉर्ड करने देने और सवाल-जवाब नहीं कराने का अनुरोध किया items.title: ‘The later it gets, the crazier the shows become’: US ambassador Sergio Gor on the chaos of Indian TV news
items.summary: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor appears to have discovered a guilty pleasure familiar to many an NRI uncle: watching Indian television news for entertainment. Speaking on a range of issues at the Economic Times World Leaders Forum in New Delhi, Gor offered what may be the most diplomatic review yet of Indian prime-time TV – marvelling at the sheer number of people who can shout simultaneously while technically being on the same programme. “I love getting back home and watching Indian TV news shows. The later it gets, the crazier the shows become. At 6 pm you have 8 people arguing on the show. At 10 pm, there are 12 people who are all speaking at the same time. You can’t hear a single one of them…it’s unbelievable that no one gets interrupted,” he said. For context: American cable news is no stranger to volume, hostility, or the occasional shouting match. But even hardened veterans of that particular arena, it seems, regard the 10-person, simultaneous-speech format of Indian prime-time as a genre of its own. Gor also used the platform to say that the Indian Ministry of External Affairs had asked for a “no-questions” arrangement ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s meeting with US President Donald Trump at the G7 summit. The meeting itself took place on June 17 on the sidelines of the G7 summit in eastern France, arriving shortly after three Indian mariners were killed when a commercial vessel came under attack by the US Navy in the Strait of Hormuz – a tragedy Modi raised directly with Trump during their conversation. According to Gor, the plan was to allow the media in only to record opening remarks, no questions permitted. Trump, briefed in advance, had signed off on it. “We were behind the scenes, behind the stage, and at one point it was just the president and I, and he asked me, he goes, what the Indians are going to raise. We went over some topics,” Gor said. “And he said, do they have any asks? And the MEA had one ask. He said, and it was, let’s bring in the media, but let’s not do a full press conference,” the ambassador added. “I told the president, I said, the Indians prefer no questions. He said, sure, no problem.” “So the meeting starts, the press comes in, there must have been 50 cameras, the president is sitting here, the prime minister is sitting there, they both speak for a few minutes,” Gor said. items.summary: In May 2020, as India was preparing to overhaul its education policy, the Narendra Modi government held a review meeting on education that placed technology at the centre, to help build what the government described as a “global knowledge super power”. Two months later, the Union Cabinet approved the National Education Policy. It made digital literacy, coding and computational thinking essential skills for every student. Coding activities were proposed to begin in the middle stage (Grades 6–8), while mathematics and computational thinking had to receive stronger focus from the foundational years. In September that year, PM Modi spoke about what education should look like in the 21st century – from coding to artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things, cloud computing, data science and robotics. But five years later, the latest 2025-26 UDISE+ (Unified District Information System for Education Plus) data presents a stark picture on digital awareness inside India’s schools. UDISE+ describes itself as the Ministry of Education’s official school education information system and says its data is collected from recognised schools and validated through administrative levels. Across India, there were 14,66,682 recognised schools in 2025-26. Of these, 10,05,245 were government schools. But only 2,56,165 government schools reported having a functional desktop computer or PC. That means just 25.5 percent of government schools had a functional desktop or PC. The national figure becomes even more striking when government schools are placed beside private unaided schools. Of the 3,41,689 private unaided schools in the country, 2,15,889 reported a functional desktop or PC. That is 63.2 percent. items.title: ‘Putting data on a server does not make it statistically useful’
items.summary: India is preparing to revamp parts of its official statistical system, conduct at least 14 surveys under the National Sample Survey Office this year, and make better use of its administrative and digital data. But, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation’s ( MoSPI ) budget for 2026-27 is 22 percent below its estimated expenses, and will not be enough to meet the physical targets of its programmes, the Ministry told a Parliamentary standing committee in a report published in March 2026. On the other hand, it had surrendered Rs 6,088 crore ($711 million) over the last three financial years. For 2026-27, MoSPI estimated expenses of Rs 5,826 crore ($625 million), but allocations in the Union budget amounted to Rs 4,522 crore ($485 million) for schemes, a shortfall of about 22 percent. Of the amount allocated, 87 percent is for the Member of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLAD), under which each MP is provided Rs 5 crore each year to support local developmental activities. The Ministry told the Committee that against an estimate of Rs 777 crore—or Rs 1 crore per district—under the Statistical Strengthening Sub-Scheme, revamped to help states generate good quality data at sub-State level, allocations stood at Rs 15 crore, based on past expenditure. The Ministry’s estimate itself was about half the requirements of Rs 1,400 crore as indicated by states and Union territories, it said. In addition, the National Sample Survey aims to conduct 14-15 surveys this year at an estimated budget of Rs 788 crore, but allocations amounted to Rs 415 crore. But money is only one part of the problem. In December 2025, the Committee's review of the National Statistical Commission had raised questions about the institution's ability to perform its oversight role. The NSC has a mandate to monitor and enforce statistical standards, but it remains a part-time body with a secretariat supported by MoSPI. How serious are these institutional and technical weaknesses, and can India's statistical system keep pace with the country’s ambitions for more granular, digital and data-driven policymaking? items.title: Rs 428 crore in, Rs 1 crore out: How Chinese capital and public money vanished into Gurugram’s garbage
items.summary: Start at the end. In the summer of 2024, a Chinese firm that runs waste-to-energy plants sold its entire Indian business for Rs 1 crore – about the price of a modest flat in the city it had been hired to clean. Seven years earlier it had bought that same business, pumped in roughly Rs 428 crore, and promised to shrink the growing landfills in Gurugram and Faridabad. Somewhere between the Rs 428 crore that went in and the Rs 1 crore that came out is the story of too many backers disappointed. And it is not a simple one, of an Indian company taking foreign investors for a ride. This is the story of that Indian firm, Ecogreen Energy Pvt Ltd, failing to deliver the Indian expansion that China Jinjiang Environment Holding Co Ltd had made it the anchor of. It is the story of a web of firms linked to Ecogreen – some the promoters’ own – in effect absorbing money meant for waste plants and garbage processing into consultancy fees, rent and inside deals. It is the story of the Bandhwari landfill, which the company was hired to shrink, climbing instead towards a mountain taller than the Aravalli slope beside it. Of the processing plant that was to transform the city, and that exists to this day only as a model made of wood and plastic. And it is the story of the bill, which the public paid whether or not anything worked. More than Rs 325 crore of taxpayers’ money went for targets that were barely met. Gurugram paid Ecogreen Rs 157 crore before it terminated the contract. Money flowed despite similar violations in other cities. Lucknow paid the company Rs 169.21 crore, according to Uttar Pradesh’s 2025 CAG report, including for a stretch when the plant it was running was shut. Gwalior in Madhya Pradesh eventually paid other agencies to do work Ecogreen was initially contracted to do. Ecogreen failed on many counts. But it is only the largest specimen of a wider habit. In the assembly, Haryana’s urban local bodies minister Vipul Goel put the government’s waste-management commitments for Gurugram and Faridabad between 2017 and 2026 at Rs 862 crore across 10 companies. When Ecogreen finally collapsed, the state had hired nine more companies on Rs 532 crore of fresh tenders simply to claw back the pile the firm had left behind – and six of those nine were themselves penalised for missing deadlines. items.title: Karnataka State Bar Council Chairman backs Manan Kumar Mishra, rejects allegations by YR Sadasiva Reddy
items.summary: The Karnataka State Bar Council (KSBC) has condemned allegations levelled against Bar Council of India (BCI) Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra by co-chairman of the BCI and former KSBC member YR Sadasiva Reddy , calling them unfounded and fuelled by political motivations. In a press release issued on August 24, KSBC nominated Chairman Kamaraddi VD said, "While the newly elected members of the KSBC await the formal takeover of office as per BCI guidelines, myself the Chairman, as the administrator of the Karnataka State Bar Council, reiterates absolute faith and confidence in favor of Shri Manan Kumar Mishra leading the Bar Council of India." Kamaraddi Venkaraddi Devaraddi YR Sadasiva Reddy had called for Mishra's resignation on the grounds that the BCI's August 13 direction (later withdrawn) to bar NALSAR graduating students from enrolment as advocates was issued without the Council's deliberation, resolution or authorisation. BCI co-chair YR Sadasiva Reddy demands resignation of BCI chairman Manan Kumar Mishra KSBC contended that Reddy's decade-long tenure in the BCI has been without objection to the functioning of the BCI and that his August 22 letter was aimed at creating friction within the legal fraternity. "His sudden, opportunistic grievances- raised years after these decisions were executed - demonstrate a clear lack of bona fides." The KSBC further stated that it had removed Reddy with a 2/3rd majority on the grounds of inefficient and unsatisfactory performance. This was 2 years after it had recommended Reddy's name as its representative on the BCI. "It is ironic that an individual previously removed by his home State Bar Council for inefficiency now seeks to question the credentials of the BCI Chairman," reads the press release. KSBC further questioned Reddy's authority as he is no longer an elected member. It claimed that he has a personal agenda in seeking Mishra's removal. Moreover, it stated, "Under the stewardship of Shri Manan Kumar Mishra, the Bar Council of India has consistently protected the autonomy of the profession, strengthened advocate welfare initiatives, upgraded digital infrastructure, and resolved institutional matters through constructive, democratic dialogue... ...We appeal to the advocates of Karnataka and across India to reject politically motivated distractions and remain united under the vision and leadership of Shri Manan Kumar Mishra." items.title: Even 0.1% of amount spent for Nashik Kumbh Mela could save Marathi medium schools: Supreme Court Justice PB Varale
items.summary: Supreme Court Justice Prasanna B Varale recently raised serious concerns over the declining budget for education in Maharashtra, contrasting the closure of State-run Marathi medium schools with the massive public expenditure on events like the Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha or Nashik Kumbh Mela. The judge was speaking at an event organised by a high school in Dhule district of Maharashtra, where had been a student for a few years. The event was an inauguration of 'smart classes'. In his address, Justice Varale highlighted how essential educational infrastructure continues to suffer despite grand government allocations for other initiatives. He referred to recent announcements regarding government expenditure on the Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha Kumbh Mela and major infrastructure corridors. “The government claims to allocate vast funds for various initiatives. The Deputy Chief Minister mentioned ₹32,000 crore and the Chief Minister mentioned ₹34,000 crore for the Kumbh Mela. I read elsewhere about ₹11,000 crore being allocated for a corridor project,” Justice Varale pointed out. He added that even a tiny fraction of such spending could revive hundreds of struggling educational institutions across the state. “I have no objection whatsoever to the thousands of crores being spent by the government on various development initiatives. However, if out of these thousands of crores of allocated funds, even just 0.1%—around ₹32 crore—were spent by the government, then 100 to 125 Marathi-medium schools that have closed down across the state would not have shut down." items.title: Kerala law student rape and murder: Supreme Court seeks State's response on plea to transfer death-row convict to Assam
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday sought the State of Kerala's response to a plea by death-row convict Muhammed Ameer-Ul-Islam seeking transfer from a Kerala jail to an Assam prison to be closer to his family [Muhammed Ameer Ul Islam v The State of Kerala & Ors.] . Ameer-Ul-Islam is the sole convict sentenced to death for the 2016 rape and murder of a Dalit law student in Kerala's Perumbavoor. A Bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Sheel Nagu was hearing his plea seeking his transfer from Viyyur Central Prison in Kerala to a jail in Assam, where his wife and aged parents reside. Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu Senior Advocate Rebecca John , appearing for Ameer-Ul-Islam, referred to Section 3 of the Transfer of Prisoners Act. She submitted that a prisoner sentenced to death cannot ordinarily be transferred without special permission from the government, except in circumstances where the prisoner's presence is required before a court. John submitted that the proceedings referred to in the provision had already concluded, pointing out that the Kerala High Court had confirmed the death sentence. "As an ordinary rule, prisoners shall not be transferred until the expiry of the appeal or until the result of the appeal is known," submitted John, adding that this stage too had passed. Senior Advocate Rebecca John The Court, however, questioned whether Assam has consented to the proposed transfer. "Where is the consent of Assam?" asked Justice Datta. John submitted that Assam is yet to consider the issue since it would decide on the request only after Kerala permits the transfer. The counsel appearing for Assam also told the Court that the State would consider the request if Kerala allows the transfer. The Court also questioned John about an amendment to the petition challenging the constitutional validity of Section 587, which restricts the transfer of prisoners, particularly those sentenced to death. John said the provision had been challenged subsequently, though not in the original petition. The Court then asked her to point out the amended prayers reflecting this challenge. The Court subsequently asked the Kerala government whether it had filed a response to the application seeking to amend the petition. The counsel for Kerala said he was not aware of the amendment. items.title: Supreme Court seeks Delhi government's response to bail plea by AAP's Naresh Balyan in MCOCA case
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday sought the Delhi government's response to a bail plea filed by Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader and former MLA Naresh Balyan in connection with a case registered under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) [ Naresh Balyan v. State NCT of Delhi ]. A Bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta issued notice on the plea challenging the Delhi High Court’s refusal to grant Balyan bail. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta He was arrested by the Crime Branch of the Delhi Police on December 4, 2024, for his alleged links to an organised crime syndicate operated by absconding gangster Kapil Sangwan alias Nandu. The prosecution has alleged that Balyan acted as a "facilitator" for Sangwan’s syndicate by identifying extortion targets, executing sham property agreements, and orchestrating forced property sales at throwaway rates. On August 3, the Delhi High Court had denied him bail in the matter, observing that there appeared to be a discernible nexus between Balyan and the crime syndicate based on intercepted mobile conversations. The High Court had also held that in cases involving serious offences under special statutes like MCOCA, prolonged incarceration alone cannot be the decisive factor for granting bail. Earlier in March, another Bench of the High Court had pulled up the Delhi Police for the delay in the probe against Naresh Balyan . At the time, the Court also directed the police to expedite the probe and place a timeline on record. Balyan has consistently refuted the allegations against him, calling the invocation of MCOCA an abuse of law and a part of a political vendetta. On July 31, a Delhi court closed an extortion case against Balyan, citing a lack of evidence.

items.title: Sex between spouses after separation does not condone matrimonial cruelty: Calcutta High Court
items.summary: Stray instances of sexual intercourse between spouses after their separation do not, by themselves, establish that earlier acts of matrimonial cruelty were condoned, the Calcutta High Court recently held. A Division Bench of Justices Sabyasachi Bhattacharyya and Supratim Bhattacharya made the observation while upholding a decree of divorce granted to a husband on the ground of mental cruelty. The Court said, “ Stray instances of sexual intercourse after separation cannot tantamount to condonation of cruelty per se .” The couple married under the Special Marriage Act on June 18, 2009 and had a child in April 2013. They separated in 2014 after matrimonial disputes arose. The husband subsequently approached a family court seeking divorce on the ground of mental cruelty. The husband alleged that the wife repeatedly made false accusations against him and his family, filed criminal complaints and insisted that he live separately from his dependent widowed mother. In December 2021, the family court granted him a divorce, prompting the wife to appeal before the Calcutta High Court. The wife had argued that she returned to the matrimonial home several times after the couple separated and lived with her husband as a spouse for 7-8 days on each occasion. According to her, this showed that the husband had forgiven the alleged cruelty. The Court rejected the argument. It held, “ Stray incidents of living together as husband and wife do not amount to condonation. ” The Bench explained that condonation was conditional on the offending spouse not committing further matrimonial offences. “ Condonation is not absolute and is impliedly conditional upon non-repetition of further acts of cruelty, either similar to the earlier acts of cruelty or otherwise, by the condoned spouse .” The Court found that the wife had made several serious but unsubstantiated allegations against her husband and his family. These included allegations of dowry demands, misappropriation of her parental property, forcible abortion and improper behaviour by her mother-in-law towards the couple’s child. The Bench said that grave, baseless allegations that demean a spouse or assassinate their character could themselves constitute mental cruelty. It also considered the wife’s demand that her husband live separately from his dependent widowed mother. items.title: Supreme Court stays Allahabad HC order for action against lawyers who fudged copy of award
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday stayed Allahabad High Court's recent order for initiation of criminal proceedings and disciplinary action against two advocates who allegedly misled the court by filing a manipulated land acquisition award mentioning higher rate of interest than the one in the original document [Shiv Kumar Mishra v Bareilly Development Authority] A Bench of Justice PK Mishra and Justice Shree Chandrashekhar also stayed the direction for lodging complaints before the Bar Council of India and the State Bar Council to seek cancellation of the advocates' licences. The interim order was passed on a petition filed by advocate Shiv Kant Mishra, one of the counsel accused of misconduct in the matter. The matter will be heard next on October 12. Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar On July 30, a Division Bench of Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Kshitij Shailendra at Allahabad had found that advocates Shiv Kant Mishra and Krishna Kant Mishra deliberately altered the contents of the award to secure monetary benefits for their client. The Court thus ruled that the advocates’ conduct prima facie attracted the offence of perjury under Section 199 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) for submitting false evidence. It directed the Registrar General to conduct an inquiry under Section 340 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) and thereafter file an appropriate complaint for perjury before the competent magistrate. Additionally, the registrar general was directed to lodge complaints before the Bar Council of India and the State Bar Council seeking cancellation of the advocates' licences “for their unpardonable conduct.” There is angst against bar and bench: Allahabad HC orders action against lawyers who filed false copy of award to mislead court The High Court also made strong observations on the legal profession, stating that people approach courts today not because they want to but only because they have no other option left “It is often said that the profession of advocacy is a noble profession however, a deep introspection is required by the bar whether anyone other than the members of the bar refer to the profession of advocacy as a noble profession anymore? items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently struck down key provisions of the Uttar Pradesh Regulation of Urban Premises Tenancy Act, 2021, holding that they were repugnant to existing central laws and lacked the required Presidential assent [ Inder Bhushan Sawhney v Kanchan Kumari Jain (Dead) and 2 Other ]. A Division Bench of Justice Saumitra Dayal Singh and Justice Swarupama Chaturvedi declared Sections 8, 9, 10, 38 and 42 of the Act ultra vires. The Court held that Sections 8, 9 and 10 – which pertain to payment of rent and its revision - were repugnant to the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. “As to the rent payable, Section 8 allows that revision of the same in terms of Section 9 and for its determination in terms of Section 10. First, revision may arise in terms of the tenancy agreement as may also the case under TPA, but then provisions exist under the Impugned Act to provide for upward revision of the rent at specified rates. Also, Section 10 provides for determination of revised rent in the case of the dispute between the landlord and the tenant i.e. lessor and lessee that is completely in conflict with the provisions of TPA,” the Bench observed. Justice Saumitra Dayal Singh and Justice Swarupama Chaturvedi It further held that Sections 38 and 42, insofar as they sought to override the procedure under the Provincial Small Causes Court Act Provincial SCC Act) and the UP Civil Laws (Amendment) Act, could not operate without prior Presidential assent. “On the procedural aspects, the Impugned Act contains a complete provision with respect to resolution of disputes by the Rent Authority. Read with Section 38 and 42 of the Impugned Act, a special forum has been created contrary to the procedure prescribed under the SCC Act read with the Civil Laws Act. It also contemplates negotiable disputes and creates a Rent Tribunal, as well. That too creates a clear repugnance with the SCC Act read with the Civil Laws Act,” the Court said. The Court passed the judgment on a batch of petitions challenging the validity of the 2021 Act, including provisions dealing with rent revision and determination by rent authorities, as well as eviction proceedings. In the judgment delivered on August 21, the Court ruled that the State legislature had not obtained Presidential assent under Article 254(2) to validate the 2021 State law. items.title: Cauvery water row: Supreme Court asks Tamil Nadu to approach CWMA over proportionate share
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday asked Tamil Nadu government to approach the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) with its grievance that Karnataka was not releasing the State’s proportionate share of Cauvery water. A Bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta was hearing the Tamil Nadu government's plea seeking directions to Karnataka for immediate release of its due share of water. Appearing for Tamil Nadu, the counsel submitted, "We have to receive proportionate quantity or water, that is unfortunately not happening." The Court noted that it had previously observed that Tamil Nadu appeared to have received more water than its allocated share from Karnataka. Today, it pointed out that the State had already received water in accordance with the CWMA's directions. “You have already received the water as directed by CWMA,” said the Court. However, the counsel for Tamil Nadu contended that the CWMA had not directed the release of the proportionate quantity of water that the State was required to receive. The Court then asked Tamil Nadu to approach the CWMA on the issue. The matter will be heard again on August 31. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta The dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu over Cauvery water dates back to two agreements in 1892 and 1924 between the erstwhile Madras Presidency and the Princely State of Mysore. After several rounds of failed negotiations, the Supreme Court directed the constitution of the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal, which gave its award in 2007, allowing Tamil Nadu to draw a fixed amount of water every day. However, the dispute continued after both States filed petitions to review the decision. In 2016, Tamil Nadu again petitioned the Supreme Court as Karnataka submitted that it had no more water to share from its reservoir. Subsequently, the top court had asked the Central government to constitute a Cauvery Management Board (CMB). In 2023, the Court declined to entertain an application by the Tamil Nadu government to increase its current share of Cauvery river water from 5,000 to 7,200 cusecs (cubic feet per second) per day. The two States have another water-sharing dispute pending before the apex court. That case concerns the Pennaiyar river . The Tamil Nadu government has filed an original suit in the matter against the Karnataka government and the Central government. items.title: Supreme Court bans construction activities within 100 meters of Rajasthan's Jojari River
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday banned all construction and development activities within 100 metres from the edge of Rajasthan's Jojari River till the conclusion of scientific determination and demarcation of the high flood line and ecological buffer zones [ In Re: 2 Million Lives At Risk, Contamination In Jojari River, Rajasthan ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta passed the order in a suo motu case concerning industrial pollution of rivers in Rajasthan, including the Jojari River. " We are of the considered view that it is necessary to put in place an interim, definite and measurable area of protection so as to adequately safeguard the riverine ecosystem during the pendency of the scientific exercise for the determination and demarcation of the high flood line and the requisite ecological buffer zones. Hence, we hereby direct that no construction or development activity of any nature whatsoever shall be permitted within a distance of 100 meters from the edge of the river in accordance with the aforesaid guidelines," the Court ordered. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta As an additional interim safeguard, the Court also ordered that no hazardous industry or polluting activity shall be permitted within 500 meters on either side of the existing flood line, wherever such flood line has been identified, or the present flow path of the river. The Court said that this arrangement will continue till the high flood line and requisite ecological buffer zones near the river are scientifically determined. The suo motu case before the Court arose after a documentary, "2 Million Lives at Risk | India's Deadliest River | Jojari, Rajasthan," exposed severe contamination in Jodhpur, Pali and Barmer districts. In November 2025, the Court revived the National Green Tribunal's 2022 clean-up directions for the Jojari, Bandi and Luni rivers and set up a high-level ecosystem oversight committee headed by former Rajasthan High Court judge Justice Sangeet Lodha. The Court has since been monitoring industrial pollution and degradation of water bodies in Rajasthan with the assistance of the committee. items.title: Trilegal enters GIFT City
items.summary: Trilegal has announced the opening of its new office in Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City), further strengthening the firm’s presence across India’s key financial and business centres. The new office reflects Trilegal’s continued investment in areas that are increasingly central to India’s cross-border financial and investment landscape. As GIFT IFSC develops into an important hub for international financial services, the firm’s presence will enable it to work more closely with financial institutions, investment funds, corporates, intermediaries and other participants operating within the ecosystem. Nishant Parikh and Sridhar Gorthi , Partners and Members of the Management Committee, Trilegal, said, “GIFT City is becoming increasingly important to how Indian and international businesses structure cross-border investments and financial transactions. As the regulatory framework and product landscape deepen, having an on-ground presence will enable us to engage more closely on the structuring and regulatory considerations that underpin these decisions.” Trilegal has been advising clients on a broad range of GIFT IFSC matters, drawing on its capabilities across banking and finance, capital markets, investment funds, corporate and M&A, financial regulatory, fintech and tax. Operating as part of Trilegal’s integrated national platform, the GIFT City office will work closely with teams across the firm to support domestic and international clients, while strengthening the firm’s presence in a market of growing importance to its clients. items.title: [Courting Controversy] AI Roulette: Can SEBI keep the chamber empty?
items.summary: “ It is madness to risk what you have and need for what you don't need. ” Warren Buffett, the Oracle of Omaha, has long cautioned against investment vehicles that offer a usually win, occasionally die payoff, likening excessive risk-taking to a game of Russian Roulette: the odds may favour you most of the time, but any one bad outcome can be catastrophic. Buffett’s warning was meant for human decision-makers, who could at least be reasoned with, restrained, or held accountable for their choices. There is, however, opacity to the risk when Artificial Intelligence (“ AI ”) and Machine Learning (“ ML ”) enter the picture. The use of AI in the stock market was recently highlighted at the 23rd FICCI Capital Markets Conference 2026, when the SEBI Chairman Mr. Tuhin Kanta Pandey, declared that SEBI was preparing guidelines for the responsible use of AI and ML in the securities market . The proposed framework is expected to follow a tiered approach, calibrating requirements to the risk posed by a given use case, and will include human oversight requirements, stronger data controls, and kill-switch mechanisms that allow AI systems to be halted quickly if they begin to behave abnormally. However, this is not a cold start. SEBI has been alive to the use of AI by market players and has been working towards designing a comprehensive framework which governs different aspects of such use. In May last year, SEBI came out with a circular for reporting AI and ML applications offered and used by Mutual Funds (“ Mutual Funds Circular ”). In order to gain an in-depth understanding of the AI and ML technologies, the Mutual Funds Circular set in place a reporting mechanism for mutual funds that were using AI or ML applications as offerings to investors or internally in their operations or to disseminate investment strategies or advice or to carry out compliance. The reporting mechanism involved detailing how an AI application was implemented and what safeguard mechanisms were in place to prevent abnormal behaviour by such applications. items.title: Central government issues guidelines for empanelling advocates as panel counsel
items.summary: The Central government has issued guidelines for empanelment of advocates as panel counsel to represent the Union of India before the Supreme Court, High Courts and various district, subordinate courts, tribunals and forums. In an Office Memorandum (OM) issued on August 20, the government has mandated the applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree in law from a university or college recognised by the Bar Council of India (BCI), be enrolled with the State Bar Council under the Advocates Act, 1961, and must have qualified the All-India Bar Examination (AIBE) with a valid certificate of practice. As per the guidelines, advocates with experience in special laws (Income Tax, Customs, GST, MLA etc.) may be considered for specialized panels representing the Union before courts, tribunals and quasi-judicial fora. Advocates having previous experience of legal work of 10 years during the government service may be considered for empanelment based on their area of expertise. Process for empanelment Applications must be submitted in the prescribed format to the Deputy Secretary, Department of Legal Affairs. The applications must include self-attested educational certificates, prior empanelment orders (if any), an undertaking to abide by the fee structures and conditions, and a declaration of no criminal conviction or professional disqualification. Tenure, disqualification and professional fee The tenure of empanelment shall be for a period of three years or until further orders, whichever is earlier. Their performance will be reviewed every year. An advocate will be disqualified from empanelment if barred under Section 24A of the Advocates Act, 1961. The advocate can also be disqualified if they have been “subject to any professional disqualification by the Bar Council or/and if they have previously abused their position as an advocate in a manner detrimental to the interests of the Union of India”. “The professional fees payable to the empanelled advocate shall be governed by the fee schedule approved by the Department of Legal Affairs, as amended or revised from time to time,” the OM states. De-empanelment and resignation The guidelines empower the Central government to de-empanel a counsel at any time for acting against instructions, failing to return briefs, misappropriation of money including court fees or costs, contempt of court, professional misconduct or conviction by a court of law. items.title: Rajasthan High Court lays down rules to prevent indiscriminate freezing of bank accounts
items.summary: The Rajasthan High Court recently laid down a framework to prevent banks and investigating agencies from indiscriminately freezing entire bank accounts during cybercrime investigations. [Balaji Enterprises v. RBI] Justice Anand Sharma directed that where the amount linked to an alleged cyber fraud is identifiable, the ordinary course should be to place a lien or hold on that amount and allow the account holder to operate the remaining balance. The petitioners had challenged the freezing, debit-freezing or lien marking of their accounts following communications from various investigating agencies. In some cases, the transaction allegedly connected with cyber fraud involved amounts below ₹100, ₹1,000, ₹5,000 or ₹10,000. However, the entire bank accounts, which contained substantially larger amounts, had been frozen. The Court said that while the State has a duty to protect cyber fraud victims and prevent the dissipation of stolen funds, investigative powers are subject to constitutional standards of legality, reasonableness and proportionality. “The seriousness of cyber-crime cannot justify abandoning the safeguards which protect an innocent citizen against arbitrary State action,” the Court stated. Justice Anand Sharma The court laid down following broad guidelines for freezing bank accounts: No indefinite blanket freeze: A bank account cannot be subjected to an indefinite, complete debit freeze based merely on a vague, unverified or cryptic communication. Record the connection between the account and the offence: Before imposing or continuing any restraint, the investigating officer must identify and record material showing a prima facie connection between the account or transaction and the offence being investigated. Ordinarily limit the restraint to the disputed amount: If the disputed amount can be identified, only that amount should ordinarily be preserved through a lien or hold. The entire account may be frozen only when reasons exist for a wider restraint. The directions in Jinat Bano must be strictly followed. Give reasons for freezing the entire account: If a complete freeze is considered necessary because of the nature of the offence, repeated transactions, mule-account indicators, the account holder’s conscious involvement or difficulty in separating the proceeds, then specific reasons must be recorded and communicated to the bank. items.title: "Political stunt": BCI Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra hits back at YR Sadasiva Reddy's call for his resignation

Speaking to ANI , Mishra dismissed Reddy’s letter as being part of a political vendetta, and also disputed references to Reddy as a BCI co-chairman. Therefore, he is no more even a member of the State Bar Council of Karnataka," Mishra said. It may be noted that the BCI’s web page for its office bearers shows Reddy as a co-chairman at the time of writing this article. Mishra further said that Reddy belong to another political party and supports Congress and his statements are borne out of political vendetta. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Saturday dismissed a plea after declining to adjourn the matter merely because the Additional Solicitor General (ASG) appearing in the case was held up in another courtroom. A Bench comprising Justice BV Nagarathna and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva made it clear that the seniority or designation of the advocate appearing made no difference to how the Court would decide a case. This was after government counsel sought adjournment in the matter, stating that ASG is on his legs in another court. "Learned ASG is held up in some other court. Please have it on Monday or Tuesday. Let him be there," the counsel said. “Whether ASG, Solicitor General, our order will be the same. It does not differ based on the advocates who appear before us. Please tell your ASG that. If Mr. Senior counsel will appear, we will pass another order? In our court, every counsel is the same,” Justice Nagarathna said. Please tell your ASG that. items.title: The GenZ effect: Why the future of law looks different
items.summary: Individuals born between 1997 and 2012 - often called Gen Z or Zoomers - are redefining norms, behaviours and expectations among the entire global legal fraternity. Law is actively shaped by the social and technological realities of a new era and today, Gen Z is doing it with their pragmatism, inclusivity and tech-savviness. They are often solution-oriented and exhibit a practical approach in tackling societal issues. This generation enters the legal profession with a deep-rooted belief that law should actually work for people. The ethos that GenZ is expected to bring to the field centres on socially conscious legal advocacy, digital fluency, work/life balance and an end to the rigid, often absurd hierarchies that still define legal practice. With this shift, the methods, expectations and values shaping law are being reinterpreted, paving the way for more diversity, innovation and authenticity in the profession. GenZ and the politics of accountability Today, law is regarded as more than a symbol of prestige, wealth, or corporate dominance. Phrases like “climate justice”, “minority rights”, “data privacy” and “accountability” are widely cited by future GenZ lawyers when questioned on why they choose to study law. This ideological shift stems from a generation that has grown up witnessing global crises on multiple forefronts . A study shows that 1 in 3 Gen Z adults engage in some form of activism or social justice work and 45% prioritise criminal justice reform, higher than their millennial counterparts (42%) and boomers (27%). This inclination reflects a belief in law’s intrinsic power to remedy injustice and that society can always be made better. Having witnessed the destruction of flora and fauna, severe urban air pollution crises, erratic climatic conditions and so on, GenZ have moved from being mere witnesses to becoming vanguards for change. Climate activist Greta Thunberg, for instance, helped organise the “School Strike for Climate” , mobilising students in 150 countries to walk out of their classrooms as a sign of protest. Further, GenZ considers climate change a “defining issue” for their generation, pursuing this commitment through social media and active participation in protests worldwide. items.title: Marriage Lite? The Supreme Court's patch notes for live-in relationships
items.summary: There is something deeply ironic about the way Indian law has approached the live-in relationship. The arrangement was, at least in part, supposed to offer consenting adults an alternative to marriage. Instead, the law has spent the better part of two decades making that alternative look increasingly like marriage - only without the wedding and the social approval. The Supreme Court’s recent judgment in Dr Lokesh BH & Ors v. State of Karnataka has pushed that evolution a little further. A Bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and NK Singh held that Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) - the cruelty provision meant for husbands - and its corresponding provision under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, can apply to a live-in relationship which is 'in the nature of marriage'. No wedding required. Only two things: a relationship that looks like a marriage and both partners genuinely meaning it to become one. The judgment is undoubtedly driven by a legitimate concern - a man should not be permitted to escape criminal liability for cruelty merely because he avoided performing a marriage ceremony. It is a judgment wrapped in progressive empathy, aiming to shield women from the technical loopholes of patriarchal legal structures. But there is a larger question here, one that sits somewhat awkwardly beside the judgment’s protective logic. By systematically importing the criminal liabilities, financial obligations and institutional surveillance of marriage into the sphere of live-in relationships, the State and the judiciary are inadvertently defeating the very purpose of non-marital cohabitation. If a live-in relationship invites the exact same legal ramifications as a marriage, why would any rational, consenting adult choose it as an alternative? At what point does protecting people in live-in relationships become an exercise in making live-in relationships legally indistinguishable from marriage? Justices Sanjay Karol and Nongmeikapam Kotiswar Singh For many urban Indians, particularly financially independent adults, the absence of marriage is the point. It can mean avoiding the legal and social baggage that comes with marriage: dowry demands, interference from extended families, expectations imposed by traditional gender roles and, perhaps most importantly, the extraordinarily cumbersome process of getting out of the relationship once it has stopped working. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday expressed its disinclination to entertain a plea filed by Matrimony.com challenging a Madras High Court judgment restraining it from using ‘Jodii’ for its matchmaking application [ Matrimony.com Limited v FreeElective Network Private Limited ]. However, instead of dismissing the plea today, a Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe gave Matrimony.com and Jodi365 an opportunity to explore an amicable resolution. Matrimony.com offered to rename its application “Jodi Matrimony” to avoid abruptly shutting down the business and affecting its existing users. The Bench asked the parties to discuss this proposal and indicated that it would consider the matter again if they were unable to arrive at a settlement. Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe The dispute arose after Matrimony.com launched its ‘Jodii’ mobile application in October 2021. FreeElective Network Private Limited, which operates the matchmaking platform Jodi365, issued a cease-and-desist notice against this move. It subsequently filed a trademark infringement and passing-off suit before the Madras High Court against Matrimony.com. FreeElective claimed that it had been using ‘Jodi365’ since 2009 and had registered it as a composite device mark in 2010. Matrimony.com countered that FreeElective's trademark registration protected only the composite ‘Jodi365’ mark and did not give FreeElective exclusive rights over the word ‘Jodi’. It argued that ‘Jodi’, meaning a couple or pair, was descriptive of matchmaking services and was widely used by other matrimonial and dating platforms. In July 2022, a single judge of the Madras High Court dismissed FreeElective’s suit. The judge found that while the composite ‘Jodi365’ mark had acquired distinctiveness, the constituent word ‘Jodi’ remained descriptive and non-distinctive. A High Court Division Bench of Justices P Velmurugan and K Govindarajan Thilakavadi, however, overturned the single-judge ruling on August 11, 2026. items.title: There is angst against bar and bench: Allahabad HC orders action against lawyers who filed false copy of award to mislead court
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court has ordered criminal proceedings and disciplinary action against two advocates who allegedly misled the court by filing a manipulated land acquisition award mentioning higher rate of interest than the one in the original document [Bareilly Development Authority v Ram Pal And 4 Others] A Division Bench of Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Kshitij Shailendra observed that advocates Shiv Kant Mishra and Krishna Kant Mishra deliberately altered the contents of the award to secure monetary benefits for their client. "Learned counsel for the respondents knew exactly what they were doing. They did it to benefit monetarily and to secure for their clients, relief that they were not entitled to under the law," the Court observed. The Court thus ruled that the advocates’ conduct prima facie attracted the offence of perjury under Section 199 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) for submitting false evidence. It directed the Registrar General to conduct an inquiry under Section 340 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) and thereafter file an appropriate complaint for perjury before the competent magistrate. Additionally, the registrar general was directed to lodge complaints before the Bar Council of India and the State Bar Council seeking cancellation of the advocates' licences “for their unpardonable conduct.” The Court also made strong observations on the legal profession, stating that people approach courts today not because they want to but only because they have no other option left “It is often said that the profession of advocacy is a noble profession however, a deep introspection is required by the bar whether anyone other than the members of the bar refer to the profession of advocacy as a noble profession anymore? Citizens approach the courts through the members of the bar out of sheer exasperation, desperation and helplessness, not because they want to, but because they have no other option," the Bench stated. An average litigant has angst against both the bar and the bench today, the Court said. "The angst of the average litigant is against both the bar and the bench. items.title: Karnataka records 4,212 influenza cases; Health Dept says H1N1 rise is seasonal
items.summary: Karnataka has recorded 4,212 laboratory-confirmed influenza cases across 32 districts so far this year, with the Health Department attributing the current rise in H1N1 cases to the state’s usual seasonal pattern and urging people not to panic. According to surveillance data from the Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP), 4,212 influenza cases had been confirmed in the state as of August 22, 2026. H1N1 is a strain of the influenza A virus that can cause seasonal flu. Common symptoms include fever, cough, sore throat, body ache and fatigue. Bengaluru accounts for the majority of the cases. The Greater Bengaluru Authority (MSU) area has reported 2,070 cases so far this year, compared to 2,587 in 2025 and 1,189 in 2024. Bengaluru Urban has recorded 1,011 cases, broadly comparable to 961 cases in 2025 and 991 in 2024. The Health Department said influenza generally records two seasonal peaks in Karnataka — between January and March and again between July and September. The current increase in cases therefore falls within the state's usual seasonal pattern. Health Department reviews preparedness Health Minister UT Khader chaired a review meeting with senior health officials from the state and districts to assess preparedness to manage the seasonal rise in influenza. The department said government health facilities have adequate infrastructure, essential medicines and other supplies to handle a possible increase in cases. Surveillance for Influenza-Like Illness (ILI) and Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) has also been strengthened in line with guidelines issued by the World Health Organization and the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. Surveillance is being carried out through designated sentinel sites under the ICMR-NCDC network for pan-respiratory virus surveillance, as well as through the Viral Research and Diagnostic Laboratories (VRDL) network. The department said laboratories have sufficient consumables to ensure timely sample collection and testing. Health facilities have been directed to maintain adequate stocks of essential supplies, including personal protective equipment, N95 masks and Oseltamivir, an antiviral medication used to treat influenza. Healthcare workers have also been sensitised to identify ILI and SARI cases early, assess risk and provide appropriate treatment. The announcement brings to an end a three-year-long protest by residents of Ekanapuram and neighbouring villages, who opposed the project over the acquisition of farmland and the displacement of residents. Environmentalists had also objected to the project, warning that it would significantly impact the area’s water resources, which include many lakes and wetlands. Announcing the scrapping of the project, Vijay said the government would identify an alternative site for Chennai’s second airport. He said a few sites had already been identified and would be assessed through scientific studies and technical feasibility assessments before a final location is selected. The Chief Minister said Chennai’s existing Meenambakkam airport, operated by the Airports Authority of India (AAI), currently handles around 30 million passengers a year. Given the city’s growing needs, he said a second airport was necessary to meet increasing passenger demand and support commercial development. However, Vijay said the second airport should not affect farmers’ livelihoods or require residents to be evicted. He accused the previous Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) government of choosing Parandur despite these concerns. “I visited Ekanapuram and other neighbouring villages in January last year and heard their demands,” Vijay told the Assembly. items.title: Chennai: OMR residents oppose Mamallan reservoir over flooding and wetland concerns
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. More than 50 organisations, including residents’ welfare associations (RWAs) from the Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) area, and over 1,100 citizens have petitioned Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay seeking the scrapping of the proposed Mamallan Reservoir project. The reservoir has been proposed as a source of drinking water for the OMR region, which continues to depend on private water tankers to meet part of its water needs. However, residents have opposed the project, citing concerns over flooding, damage to wetlands and its possible impacts on local livelihoods. Harsha Koda, co-founder of the Federation of OMR Residents’ Welfare Association (FOMRRA), said OMR’s residential areas are located between two important wetland systems — the Pallikaranai marsh and the Nemmeli wetlands. “This reservoir project will heighten flood risk and significantly aggravate our climate vulnerability,” he said. Residents have also raised concerns that the project could alter the drainage patterns of the Pallikaranai and Kovalam marshland catchments, which eventually drain into the sea through the Kovalam estuary. According to them, areas including Sholinganallur, Perumbakkam, Navalur, Siruseri and Thazhambur, which are drained by the Pallikaranai catchment, could face greater flood risks during intense rainfall. Thaiyur and Padur, which fall within the Kovalam catchment, could also face seawater flooding, they said. Koda also claimed that water levels in the Buckingham Canal had increased, alleging that the canal had been blocked for construction related to the Mamallan Reservoir. Residents are also concerned about the Kovalam-Nemmeli salt marsh, which they allege could be affected by the project. According to them, the wetland provides a habitat for more than 200 resident and migratory bird species. Instead, the residents have urged the government to protect existing water bodies, prevent encroachments and promote rainwater harvesting. They have also sought a transparent water allocation policy and drinking water projects based on scientific assessments that do not compromise wetlands or natural drainage channels.

items.title: Kerala: DYFI protests in DRM office over Palakkad railway division split
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI), the youth wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)], launched a protest on Monday, August 24, against the Indian Railways Board's decision to split the Palakkad Railway Division. DYFI blocked the Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) office in Palakkad as part of the protest. The Railway Board decided to detach the Mangaluru region from the Palakkad Railway Division and merge it with Mysuru. The decision will take effect from October 1. The move is expected to significantly undermine the operational and financial importance of Palakkad Division. DYFI protesters raised slogans against the Union government and the Railway Board, calling the bifurcation an anti-people move that harms Kerala. DYFI began their protest at 7.30 am, and police tried to stop them from entering the officers' building. “We will continue our protest. We have decided to continue the protest by detaining the officials here. No matter how large a police force is deployed, we have the strength to overcome it,” a DYFI leader told the media . The Railway Board’s decision has sparked opposition in Kerala, with many political leaders, including Chief Minister VD Satheesan, openly criticising the move. Chief Minister Satheesan said the Railway Board's unilateral decision is unacceptable. CPI(M) Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas urged the Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw to completely withdraw the planned transfer. Meanwhile, speaking with the media on Sunday, August 23, Kasaragod MP Rajmohan Unnithan said that Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw informed the Kerala MPs that he was unaware of the Railway Board decision. “The Minister told us he came to know about the issue only after the Kerala government informed them of their protest over the decision. He also said he will recheck the decision. But we will not believe what he said, as a decision like this won't come without informing the Minister. Railway cannot take this decision alone,” he added.

items.title: Kerala: Ex-BJP leader KK Padmarajan gets bail in Palathayi POCSO case
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has granted bail to KK Padmarajan, a schoolteacher and former Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment in the Palathayi sexual assault case. The court held that there was prima facie an infirmity in the conviction order and that he had made out a “good case on merits” in his appeal. A division bench comprising Justices Raja Vijayaraghavan V and KV Jayakumar passed the order on August 20 while considering Padmarajan’s application seeking suspension of his sentence pending his appeal against the November 2025 conviction by the Special Judge of the Fast Track Special Court, Thalassery. The court’s order places considerable emphasis on what it described as inconsistencies in the evidence of the survivor, who was 10 years and six months old at the time of the alleged incidents. “On a preliminary analysis of the evidence of PW1, the victim, prima facie, we find that the victim had an inconsistent, embellished, improved and fanciful version about the alleged sexual abuse,” the court said. The case relates to Padmarajan, who was the BJP’s former Thrippangottur panchayat president and a Malayalam teacher at a school in Palathayi, who was accused of taking the girl to a school washroom on multiple occasions and sexually assaulting her. According to the prosecution case recorded in the High Court order, the incidents allegedly took place on a day before January 15, 2020, and on January 15 and February 2 that year. The Panoor police registered a case on March 17, 2020, based on the girl’s statement. The trial court had convicted Padmarajan under Sections 376(2)(f), 376AB and 354B of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) (rape of a girl below 12, aggravated rape and assault) and Sections 5(f), 5(l), 5(m) read with Section 6 (aggravated penetrative sexual assault by a relative or person in authority, and against a child below 12) of POCSO. It sentenced him to imprisonment for the remainder of his natural life under Section 376AB of the IPC, besides 20 years’ rigorous imprisonment each for offences under the POCSO Act. While considering the suspension of the sentence, the High Court focused on the alleged place of occurrence, noting that the school toilet was “very close to the classrooms” and that the school itself was situated on a small extent of property. The bench also referred to differences in the medical evidence. The girl was initially examined by Dr Vasumathi, who did not record any evidence of sexual assault.
